summary.en-US: Click the toolbar button, show a QR code to your camera, get copyable text. Fully offline: decoding runs locally in Rust/WebAssembly.

description.en-US:
qrqrqr scans QR codes with your webcam straight from the toolbar and shows the decoded text in a box you can copy or edit.

• Works offline: the decoder (the Rust crate rqrr, compiled to WebAssembly) ships inside the extension.
• No permissions, no network requests, no data collection.
• Reads inverted (light-on-dark) codes too.
• Optionally reads the 6-digit code of an authenticator app shown on a phone (offline OCR: the pure-Rust ocrs engine and its model ship inside the extension).
• Pick between several cameras.

First use: Firefox cannot show the camera permission prompt inside a toolbar popup, so qrqrqr offers to open itself in a tab once. Allow the camera there and tick “Remember this decision”.

Source code and build instructions: https://github.com/fenollp/qrqrqr

version.approval_notes: The .wasm file is compiled from the Rust code in src/ (attached source zip). Build: install Rust stable + `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` + `cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.100`, then run `make wasm models`. Output goes to extension/pkg/ and extension/models/. The OCR model file in extension/models/ (text-recognition.rten) is the unmodified pretrained model of https://github.com/robertknight/ocrs-models (CC-BY-SA 4.0), downloaded and sha256-verified by `make models`; they are bundled in the extension and read locally, never downloaded at runtime. The camera permission is a web permission requested via getUserMedia; there are no extension permissions.
